summary: Takao Moriyasu was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He served as an associate professor at Kanazawa University and was a professor at Osaka University from 1994 to 2012.

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Takashi Iwata studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Ernst Steinkellner, Akira Hirakawa, Albrecht Wezler, and Lambert Schmithausen. He served as associate professor and professor at Waseda University.
Takashi Koezuka is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at Osaka University, serving as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2012).
Takashi Maeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 1995 and 2006.

Takashi Matsuura is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Tokyo. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo in 2022 alongside various part-time lecturing positions.

Takashi Nakao was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He was an associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College and served as an emeritus professor at Rissho University from 1979 to 2002.

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He served as an associate professor at Komazawa University (1991) and specially appointed professor at Tokyo International University (2024).
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute, Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takatsugu Hayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi. His posts include positions at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi was an archaeology and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and served as its professor of archaeology (~1953–1983). He later directed Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, Sen-oku Matsurokan, the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, and the Research Centre for Silk Roadology.

Takayasu Kimura is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. Attested in 1995, he served as a lecturer at Taisho University and researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (attested 2014–2015).

Takayoshi Kamei was a history and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Ibaraki University (~1949–1952), and Seisen University, and he taught Hajime Nakamura.

Takayoshi Namikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his undergraduate and doctoral education at Bukkyo University. He was appointed professor at Bukkyo University in 1981 and became professor emeritus in 2018.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as a faculty member and later professor (attested 2014) at Taisho University.

Takehiro Sueki was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1952–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University. He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and as a university assistant (1948–1977), later becoming a professor at Otemon Gakuin University and professor and president at Otemae University.
